To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Samantha Lee <sam.lee@fintechco.com>

Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo — Logging & sensitive data redaction (post-call recap & next steps)

Hi Alex / Sam —

Thanks again for taking the time to run through your logging & privacy requirements earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared action plan.

Call highlights (from our side):
- FintechCo needs assurance that request/response logs and headers do not retain PII or sensitive identifiers (customer IDs, account numbers, SSNs).
- Your security team asked specifically about trace IDs, header values, and full-response retention windows.
- You prefer field-level redaction where possible, with the ability to hash or drop certain identifiers for analytics.
- Data residency: US-only processing for production traffic is a hard requirement for the initial pilot.

Immediate next steps (owners):
1) Monica (Security) to share our logging controls matrix and redaction policy examples (we'll attach a short matrix + policy).
2) I will follow up with a short proposal that includes config options (field redaction, retention TTLs, header scrubbing) and a rough cost delta for enabling full-request logging masking.
3) Schedule a technical deep dive with your infra/security folks to walk through examples and test vectors (suggest next Tue/Wed).

Requested items from FintechCo:
- Example log lines (sanitized) showing the worst-case fields you want removed/hashed.
- Compliance checklist items that are must-haves vs nice-to-haves.

I'll attach our matrix in the follow-up from Monica. Please flag anything I missed.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0192

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A couple quick clarifying Qs from our security team: 
- Can you confirm whether trace IDs are stored as-is in our logs or if they can be hashed/rotated? We need to ensure traceability for debugging but not expose customer identifiers.
- Do you support scrubbing of headers (Authorization, Cookie, X-Forwarded-For) by default or as a config flag?
- For request bodies, can we set retention TTLs per route / model? For some endpoints we want 7-day retention only.

I'll try to share a couple sanitized examples of our current logs by EOD. We also need any SOC2 evidence or sample audit controls you can share.

Appreciate it,
Alex Johnson
Platform Security Lead, FintechCo
alex.johnson@fintechco.com

Alex / Marissa —

Following up with the controls matrix and a short summary of capabilities. Attaching: redaction_policy.pdf (summary) and logging_controls_matrix.xlsx (config matrix).

Key capabilities that map to your asks:
- Field-level redaction: We support rule-based and ML-assisted PII detection to redact or mask fields in request/response bodies. Rules can be scoped per route.
- Header scrubbing: Built-in policies to drop or replace Authorization, Cookie, X-Forwarded-For, and any custom headers. This is configurable per environment.
- Trace IDs: By default we retain trace IDs for debugging; however, we can hash or pseudonymize them at ingestion. We offer a hashed-trace mode where the original ID is never stored unencrypted — only a one-way hash is kept for correlation.
- Retention TTLs: Per-route retention TTLs are supported (7 days / 30 days / customer-configurable). Shorter retention can be enforced for production.
- Request/response logging modes: none / metadata-only / full-with-redaction. You can choose metadata-only for high-sensitivity routes.
- Data residency: Hosted US regions only for your production traffic; alternate option to deploy in your VPC/private instance for complete control.

SOC2 & audit items:
- We can provide SOC2-in-scope logging policies and relevant control narratives.
- Logging_controls_matrix.xlsx maps each control to evidence we can provide (config snapshots, redaction rules, and audit logs).

Next steps:
- Marissa: we should share a short config proposal and sample masked vs unmasked log examples.
- Alex: if you can share sanitized sample logs, we will prepare matching redaction rules and show sample outputs.

Attachments: redaction_policy.pdf, logging_controls_matrix.xlsx

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com

Alex —

Thanks for the quick follow-up. A couple operational notes from our side:
- Timeline: if you can share sanitized logs by Tue EOD, Monica and her team can produce example outputs by Thu.
- Cost: enabling full-request redaction + shorter retention TTLs has a modest delta; Marissa will include a rough estimate in the proposal. If you prefer to avoid hosted retention entirely, we can propose a Dedicated/Private deployment option (higher fixed cost but zero hosted retention).
- Technical deep dive: propose Tue 2027-08-10 10:00 AM PT. We'll invite infra and SRE folks.

Proposed next steps (concrete):
1) Alex: send 2-3 sanitized log samples (worst-case examples) — target Tue EOD.
2) Monica: produce masked examples + redaction rule set — target Thu.
3) Marissa: send proposal with config options and cost delta — target Thu.
4) All: deep dive Tue 2027-08-10 10:00 AM PT (tentative) — calendar invite to follow.

If that works, we'll move forward.

Best,
David Kim
Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference
